figures: 1. Figure 1: Comprehensive performance comparison across detection methods. The three academic approaches substantially outperform traditional baselines, but with surprisingly small differences among themselves. Error bars indicate 95% confidence intervals computed through bootstrap resampling.

2. Figure 2: Confusion matrices reveal distinct error patterns across methods. PhishIntention shows higher false positives, potentially due to aggressive brand matching. The feature ensemble achieves the most balanced performance with minimal errors in both directions.

3. Figure 3: Feature importance analysis reveals URL-based features as most discriminative for phishing detection. URL length and special character patterns provide the strongest signals, while semantic features like brand mentions show lower but still significant importance.

4. Figure 4: Ablation study revealing SHARP's component contributions and adaptive threshold optimization. Left: Component-wise F1-scores show synergistic gains. Right: Adaptive thresholds outperform fixed thresholds across all settings.

5. Figure 5: ROC curves demonstrate superior discrimination capability of academic methods compared to baselines. The feature ensemble achieves the highest AUC (0.95), though all academic methods show strong performance across the full range of decision thresholds.
results_section: 1. SHARP achieves the highest F1-score (0.957), surpassing the previous state-of-the-art feature ensemble (0.934) by 2.3% and CNN-BiGRU (0.915) by 4.2%.
2. This performance gain is statistically significant (p < 0.001, McNemar's test).
3. SHARP achieves exceptional performance with precision of 0.968 and recall of 0.947.
4. The feature ensemble follows with precision 0.946 and recall 0.923.
5. CNN-BiGRU shows precision 0.903 and recall 0.927.
6. PhishIntention exhibits conservative detection with precision 0.912 but lower recall 0.869.
7. Traditional baselines (F1: 0.745 and 0.649) lag significantly but show high precision when triggered, validating our hybrid approach.
8. SHARP requires 3.2 seconds average processing with 1.5 MB footprint.
9. The cascaded architecture: 65% of emails classified by regex in <10ms, 30% require LLM analysis (~1s), 5% invoke full pipeline.
10. PhishIntention: 0.52s/0.1MB but lower accuracy.
11. CNN-BiGRU: 45.2s/12.4MB (14× slower).
12. Feature ensemble: 23.8s/8.6MB (7× slower).
13. PhishIntention: 18 false positives from legitimate financial emails triggering dual indicators, 13 false negatives from sophisticated attacks avoiding brands.
14. CNN-BiGRU: 15 FP, 10 FN randomly distributed.
15. Feature ensemble: 12 FP, 8 FN (most balanced), errors on bulk emails and mimicry attacks.
16. URL-based features dominate importance rankings: URL length (0.82) and special character ratio (0.75) provide the strongest signals.
17. Domain reputation (0.68) and keyword count (0.65) form the next tier.
18. Surprisingly, HTTPS usage (0.58), form elements (0.48), and credential requests (0.42) show lower importance, suggesting future systems should prioritize URL and domain analysis.
19. Our ROC analysis shows the feature ensemble achieving the highest AUC (0.95), followed by CNN-BiGRU (0.93) and PhishIntention (0.91), all substantially outperforming the baseline (0.78).
20. [Feature ensemble ROC] achieving 90% true positive rate with only 3% false positives.
21. LLM-Only Configuration: Using only the LLM achieves 0.918 F1-score.
22. Fixed Threshold: Using fixed rather than adaptive thresholds reduces F1-score to 0.927.
23. The 3.9% improvement over LLM-only and 30.8% over regex-only configurations validates our synergistic design philosophy.
